**Brulion {{VERSION}}** — Markdown notes that work offline: block outlines and a daily journal (like Logseq) on plain `.md` files (like Obsidian), tasks, a calendar, reminders with alarms, calculations and tables. Sync through Syncthing or Nextcloud.

**What's new in {{VERSION}}**

* **Notes in Inter** — note text is now set in Inter, the interface's font, by default, with a real bold italic too; Literata stays a tap away (Settings → Editor → Font → Serif), and a font you chose before stays.

From version 0.19.0: AI that knows your whole notebook (and changes it when you say yes), ignoring a page's tasks, and `b.search`, `b.query` and `b.ai` with tools for extensions. From version 0.18.1: a tap on a date to change it (and "+" for a separate reminder), AI a tap away on the top bar and settings in tabs on the phone. From version 0.18.0: extensions in your notebook, the Luau console, AI also on the phone, pages opening faster and workout exercises out of Tasks. From version 0.17.0: the gym and a date, a reminder or an alarm in the date dialog. From version 0.16.4: adding a date to a task in one tap and Search ready for typing. From version 0.16.3: views ready from the start and reminders that stay chips while you edit. From version 0.16.2: safer links to files and folders, limits that keep hostile notes harmless and faster Dataview. From version 0.16.1: notebooks on GitHub, Dataview queries from Obsidian, a new alarm screen on Android, the browser version straight from the download page, task time kept by the Logseq import and instant switching between views. From version 0.15.0: reading mode on the top bar, menus by keyboard, every command in the / menu, picking a day in the agenda, Back zooming out first on Android, safer deleting, dialogs that say what is wrong and the download page. From version 0.14.1: reading mode, wheel scrolling like in a web browser, bottom navigation with views only, calendar icons on phones, smoother long pages, a smaller app and more visible graph links. From version 0.13.1: the “Nocny” look, built-in fonts, the side panel in sections and as a drawer on phones, the status bar and the journals folder in All pages. From version 0.12.1: subtasks under their task and folding them, the documentation in English, ☰ always first on phones, smoother scrolling and the tray calendar with one click on Linux. From version 0.11.2: the interface compiled to native code. From version 0.10.3: an intro on the first start, reminders from other devices checked in the background on Android, the view bar and the **Search or type a command…** field at the top, the new **More** menu, Brulion's own F-Droid repository and the browser version in a single file. From version 0.9.1: tabs, split view and separate windows, spell checking, link preview, weekly and monthly notes, searching the journal across many days, habits, task dependencies and time tracking, sorting, filtering and CSV in tables, charts, printing and exporting a page to PDF and Word without Pandoc, text selection, the outline and links in the PDF viewer, a page icon and cover, coloured highlights, statistics and focus mode, custom keyboard shortcuts and new drawing tools. From version 0.8.1: Mermaid diagrams, automatic backups, find and replace (in a note and in the whole notebook), clickable parts of a nested tag and deleting with undo. From version 0.7.0: more shapes, handles to resize and rotate and the **Style** panel in drawings, inserting and moving table rows and columns, **Clean up** (notes and attachments that nothing leads to) and a new-version notice on Android and Windows. From version 0.6.3: a custom drawing background colour. From version 0.6.2: any file as a link (`/File…`). From version 0.6.1: PDF preview and a PDF viewer in the app, clickable parts of a link to a page in a folder. From version 0.6.0: a refreshed look, editing page properties, a dark background, shapes, text and lasso in drawings, drawing on slides and PDFs, Obsidian drawings (`*.excalidraw.md`), merging drawing conflicts, "Open with → Brulion" on Windows and Linux, a faster and lighter index, faster undo, a smooth graph, a smaller app. From version 0.5.0: drawings in notes, Android widgets, "Share → Brulion", **Done** in a reminder's notification, native notifications, autostart and a tray calendar on Windows, appearance settings, menus on date tokens and links, import from Microsoft To Do. From version 0.4.5: pictures from the internet in notes and the first (test) version for Windows. From version 0.4.4: export for Pandoc (one `.md` document of a notebook, a folder or a page — for Word, LibreOffice, PDF and EPUB). From version 0.4.2: changing a date from a menu (right-click or long-press a date token). From version 0.4.1: the "Select text" view removed (copy by selecting whole blocks). From version 0.4.0: moving and creating folders (with links updated and folders synced to Nextcloud), tags as links to pages, copying links to bullets and headings, selecting and copying groups of blocks, a toolbar above the keyboard on phones, and the `brulion-cli` command line and an MCP server for AI agents. From version 0.3.7: the list of all changes in the documentation. From version 0.3.6: choosing a task's status from a menu and with the "/" command, emoji in the browser instead of empty squares, and security and stability fixes in formulas, code blocks, the documentation, Nextcloud and images. From version 0.3.5: picking the time on a round clock face. From version 0.3.4: images and attachments shown as pictures. From version 0.3.3: math formulas drawn right in notes. From version 0.3.2: switching notebooks with one click. From version 0.3.1: Nextcloud sync tied to a notebook. From version 0.3.0: documentation written in Brulion and quick notebook switching.

**Highlights**

* Two note modes: an **outline** (indented blocks, folding, zooming in — like Logseq) and a **document** (continuous text with a live preview — like Obsidian). You choose the mode when you create a page and can change it any time; it is stored in the note's frontmatter (`brulion: document`).
* A journal page for every day, `[[…]]` links, tags, block references `((…))`, backlinks, a graph, search (diacritics optional) with replace, version history, a trash and automatic backups.
* Tasks with due dates, a calendar (month, week, agenda), reminders ⏰ and alarms ⏰! — on Android they work with the app closed and after the phone restarts. Dates can be typed in plain English or Polish ("tomorrow 9:00", "next friday 6pm", "jutro o 9").
* Calculations in `calc` blocks (units, currencies, percentages) and tables with formulas.
* Sync: Syncthing (a plain folder, conflict copies merged), Nextcloud/WebDAV (in the background, three-way merge, a guard against mass deletion) or a GitHub repository (new versions merged, commits and pull requests when you ask).
* Import from Obsidian, Logseq, Notion, Evernote, Google Keep, Microsoft To Do, Joplin, Simplenote, Roam, Bear, Trilium, Markdown, HTML and iCalendar; export to 12 formats (including PDF, Word and a document for Pandoc) and printing.
* English and Polish interface, dark and light themes, your own accent colour and fonts.
* Drawings in notes: a pen with stylus pressure, shapes, text, a dark background, drawing on slides and PDFs; SVG files that Obsidian shows and excalidraw.com opens for editing.
* Android: home-screen widgets and "Share → Brulion".

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Android 9 or later (arm64) | `brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-arm64-v8a.apk` — or the F-Droid repository {{PAGES_URL}} (the same APK, updates through F-Droid) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-x86_64.AppImage` — Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+ (glibc ≥ 2.35) |
| Linux aarch64 (e.g. Raspberry Pi 4/5 with a 64-bit system) | `Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-aarch64.AppImage` — Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13+, Fedora 40+ (glibc ≥ 2.39) |
| Windows 10/11 (x86_64) — test version | `Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` (installer) or `brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64.zip` (portable) |
| NixOS | flake `github:{{REPO}}/{{TAG}}`, package `brulion` |
| Command line (Linux, Windows) | `brulion-cli` — in the AppImage as `./Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-x86_64.AppImage cli …`, with Nix `nix run github:{{REPO}}/{{TAG}}#brulion-cli -- …`, on Windows `brulion-cli.exe` next to `brulion.exe` |
| Browser | nothing to download: {{PAGES_URL}}app/ — or `brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.html`, a single file you open from disk, or `brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.zip` for your own server (any directory, HTTPS) |
| Source code | `brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-source.tar.gz` |

**Installation**

* **Android:** download the `.apk` file on your phone and open it (the first time, the system asks you to allow installing apps from that source). A new version installs over the previous one without losing your notes. Or add Brulion's repository in F-Droid ({{PAGES_URL}}: the "Add to F-Droid" button or the QR code) — updates then come through F-Droid.
* **Linux (AppImage):** `chmod +x Brulion-*.AppImage`, then `./Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-x86_64.AppImage` (or `…-aarch64.AppImage`). When the system reports a FUSE error (e.g. in a container): `./Brulion-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run`.
* **Windows (test version):** run `Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` — it installs for the current user only, without administrator rights (uninstalling keeps your notes and settings). The app is not signed, so SmartScreen warns: "More info" → "Run anyway". Portable version: unpack `brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64.zip` and run `brulion.exe` from the `Brulion` folder. Reminders and alarms are Windows notifications; the settings can start Brulion when you sign in.
* **NixOS:** `nix run github:{{REPO}}/{{TAG}}` or the flake's package in your system configuration.
* **Browser:** open {{PAGES_URL}}app/ (**Open in the browser** on the download page) — nothing to download or install; it works offline after the first visit, "Install app" in the browser's menu makes it an app, and your notes stay in that browser. Or download `brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.html` and open it in a browser (double-click it or drag it into the window) — it works without a server and without internet, and your notes stay in the browser also after you download a newer version of the file. On your own server (`brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.zip`) choose "Install app" — it works offline too.

SHA-256 checksums: `SHA256SUMS.txt` (`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`).

**Najważniejsze**

* Dwa tryby notatki: **konspekt** (bloki z wcięciami, zwijanie, przybliżanie — jak w Logseq) i **dokument** (ciągły tekst z podglądem na żywo — jak w Obsidianie). Tryb wybierasz przy tworzeniu strony i możesz go zmienić w każdej chwili; zapisuje się w nagłówku notatki (`brulion: document`).
* Dziennik na każdy dzień, linki `[[…]]`, tagi, odwołania do bloków `((…))`, odnośniki zwrotne, graf, wyszukiwarka (także bez polskich znaków) z zamianą, historia wersji, kosz i automatyczne kopie zapasowe.
* Zadania z terminami, kalendarz (miesiąc, tydzień, agenda), przypomnienia ⏰ i alarmy ⏰! — na Androidzie działają przy zamkniętej aplikacji i po restarcie telefonu. Daty można wpisywać po polsku („jutro o 9”, „w piątek 18:00”).
* Obliczenia w blokach `calc` (jednostki, waluty, procenty) i tabele z formułami.
* Synchronizacja: Syncthing (zwykły folder, scalanie kopii konfliktów), Nextcloud/WebDAV (w tle, scalanie trójstronne, ochrona przed masowym usuwaniem) albo repozytorium GitHub (scalanie nowych wersji, commity i pull requesty, kiedy o nie poprosisz).
* Import z Obsidiana, Logseq, Notion, Evernote, Google Keep, Microsoft To Do, Joplin, Simplenote, Roam, Bear, Trilium, Markdown, HTML i iCalendar; eksport do 12 formatów (m.in. PDF, Word i dokument dla programu Pandoc) oraz druk.

* Android: widżety na ekranie głównym i „Udostępnij → Brulion”.

**Instalacja**

* **Android:** pobierz plik `.apk` na telefonie i otwórz go (pierwszy raz system poprosi o zgodę na instalowanie aplikacji z tego źródła). Nowa wersja instaluje się na poprzednią bez utraty notatek. Albo dodaj w F-Droid repozytorium Brulionu ({{PAGES_URL}}: przycisk „Add to F-Droid” albo kod QR) — wtedy aktualizacje przychodzą przez F-Droid.
* **Linux (AppImage):** `chmod +x Brulion-*.AppImage`, a potem `./Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-x86_64.AppImage` (albo `…-aarch64.AppImage`). Gdy system zgłasza błąd FUSE (np. w kontenerze): `./Brulion-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run`.
* **Windows (wersja testowa):** uruchom `Brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` — instaluje się tylko dla bieżącego użytkownika, bez uprawnień administratora (odinstalowanie zostawia notatki i ustawienia). Aplikacja nie jest podpisana, więc SmartScreen ostrzega: „Więcej informacji” → „Uruchom mimo to”. Wersja przenośna: rozpakuj `brulion-{{FILE_VERSION}}-windows-x86_64.zip` i uruchom `brulion.exe` z folderu `Brulion`. Przypomnienia i alarmy są powiadomieniami Windows; w ustawieniach włączysz uruchamianie po zalogowaniu.
* **NixOS:** `nix run github:{{REPO}}/{{TAG}}` albo pakiet z flake'a w konfiguracji systemu.
* **Przeglądarka:** otwórz {{PAGES_URL}}app/ („Otwórz w przeglądarce” na stronie pobierania) — bez pobierania i instalowania; po pierwszym otwarciu działa offline, „Zainstaluj aplikację” w menu przeglądarki robi z niej aplikację, a notatki zostają w tej przeglądarce. Albo pobierz `brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.html` i otwórz go w przeglądarce (dwuklik albo przeciągnięcie do okna) — działa bez serwera i bez internetu, notatki zostają w przeglądarce także po pobraniu nowszej wersji pliku. Na własnym serwerze (`brulion-web-{{FILE_VERSION}}.zip`) wybierz „Zainstaluj aplikację” — działa też offline.

Sumy kontrolne SHA-256: `SHA256SUMS.txt` (`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`).
